newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says could unblock BOP aid for Romania.
newsitem.headline: EU says could unblock BOP aid for Romania.

text.p: The European Union's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Monday the EU could unblock 70 million Ecus in balance of payments aid for Romania once the country had reached an agreement with the International Monetary Fund in loan talks.

He also said, after he and European Commissioner President Jacques Santer met Romania's new President Emil Constantinescu, that the Union would favour a new balance of payments assistance programme from the international donor community once Romania's reform process was really being working.
"The 70 million Ecus blocked for some time could, after discussions with the IMF, be unblocked by the ministers of the EU," he told reporters.
"I think that the international donor community should then be prepared in case the reform is really being implemented to see whether additional BOP assistance should be given."
He stressed that for such a new package the donor community, including the G-24, the World Bank and the IMF, would "have to be convinced that the reforms are working."

Commission President Santer indicated to reporters that Romania's reform process since Constantinescu took over were highly thought of in Brussels, where the EU is considering Romania's bid for membership.
